title: 1789 Capital and Vulcan Elements
summary: Don Jr. is a 1789 Capital partner. The firm passed $1B in assets in September 2025 and later grew to roughly $2-3.5B. The NYT reported returns of roughly 200% as of mid-2026. 1789 invested in Vulcan Elements in August 2025, about three months before a $1.4B government-backed package that included a $620M Pentagon Office of Strategic Capital loan. ProPublica did report that the deal was the only one initiated by a top White House aide (Peter Navarro) and quoted 'The call came from the White House: We have to get this done.' The video compresses the timing, calls the loan a 'contract', and implies Don Jr. anticipated or arranged the deal, which no reporting documents; he and 1789 deny any role.

sub_claims.statement: Don Jr. is a partner at 1789 Capital.
sub_claims.finding: He joined as a partner in November 2024. The firm was co-founded by Omeed Malik, with Chris Buskirk. He reportedly does not sit on the growth fund's investment committee.

sub_claims.statement: 1789 Capital has over $1 billion in assets.
sub_claims.finding: Reuters reported over $1B on 2025-09-08. Later 2026 reporting puts it at about $2B (growth fund) to about $3.5B in total, plus a $1.2B real-estate fund closed in August 2026, so the video's figure is dated and understated.

The NYT (Maureen Farrell, 2026-07-22) reported roughly or nearly 200% returns for the main fund as of 2026-06-30, driven largely by Polymarket. These are unrealized, early-stage figures; PitchBook puts the average for 2023-vintage funds at about 21%.

sub_claims.statement: 1789 invested in Vulcan Elements shortly before Vulcan announced a ~$1B, 10,000-metric-ton magnet facility enabled by a US government partnership.
sub_claims.finding: 1789 joined Vulcan's $65M Series A in August 2025, reportedly at about a $200M valuation. On 2025-11-03 Vulcan, ReElement and the Department of War/Commerce announced a $1.4B package: a $620M OSC loan to Vulcan, $50M in CHIPS incentives, an $80M OSC loan to ReElement, about $550M in private capital, and government warrants or equity, for a 10,000 t/yr magnet plant. The site in Benson, NC (about $918M) was announced on 2025-11-18. The gap was about three months, not 'right before'.

sub_claims.statement: 1789 profits by investing in companies that get government contracts, which Don Jr. is skilled at anticipating.
sub_claims.finding: Several portfolio companies have won federal money, and Don Jr.-linked Unusual Machines was under review for its own Pentagon loan. But no reporting documents that Don Jr. had foreknowledge or was involved. Vulcan's award was a loan with warrants, not a contract.

sub_claims.statement: ProPublica reported 'the call came from the White House: we have to get this deal done' and that Vulcan's was the only deal initiated by a top aide to the president.
sub_claims.finding: ProPublica (Robert Faturechi, 2026-05-28) reported that White House adviser Peter Navarro, described as a friend of Don Jr., initiated the deal. A Pentagon official is quoted: 'The call came from the White House: We have to get this done.' The video inserts the word 'deal'. Of the dozens of companies under consideration, Vulcan's was the only one initiated by a top presidential aide, and it closed in weeks rather than months.

sub_claims.statement: 1789 says it is a passive minority growth-equity investor and does not call the government.
sub_claims.finding: This is the firm's stated position. 1789 told ProPublica it played no role and did not know of the loan before it was public. A Trump Jr. spokesperson said he does not discuss portfolio companies with officials and did not speak to Navarro about Vulcan. The exact quoted wording and the speaker in the clip could not be independently located.

corrections: Transcript says 1789 bought 'right before' the government got involved; it invested in August 2025, about three months before the 2025-11-03 announcement.
Transcript frames it as a Pentagon 'contract'; it was a $620M Office of Strategic Capital direct loan (initially conditional) plus $50M in Commerce CHIPS incentives and government warrants or equity.
Transcript quotes 'We have to get this deal done'; ProPublica's quote is 'The call came from the White House: We have to get this done.'
Transcript says 'over one billion dollars in assets'; that was the September 2025 figure, and 2026 reports put 1789 at about $2-3.5B.
Transcript says returns of 'over 200 percent'; the NYT reported roughly or nearly 200% (unrealized) as of 2026-06-30.
ProPublica identifies the White House aide who initiated the deal as Peter Navarro, not Don Jr. or 1789.
denials_and_context: Pentagon: 'outside affiliations, investors, or political connections play absolutely no role in the Department's funding decisions.'

1789 Capital says it played no role in the loan and learned of it only when it was public; a Trump Jr. spokesperson says he never spoke to Navarro about Vulcan, and NYT coverage says Trump Jr. claims never to have met or spoken with anyone at Vulcan.
Vulcan CEO John Maslin told reporters and House staff (2026-04-16) there was no political favoritism; House Democrats say ProPublica's account contradicts this.
Navarro reportedly called the reporting 'fake news' and defended the startups on supply-chain-resilience grounds.

Rare-earth magnets are a genuine national-security bottleneck given China's dominance and export controls, and the package drew about $550M in private capital, so there is a policy rationale independent of 1789.
No evidence has been published that Don Jr. or 1789 lobbied for the loan; the documented intervention is Navarro's.
ReElement withdrew from its $80M conditional OSC loan process in July 2026.
